title: Improving Adversarial Data Collection by Supporting Annotators: Lessons from GAHD, a German Hate Speech Dataset
measurement_description: The paper measures the detection of hate speech, which is defined as abusive or discriminatory language directed at a protected group. Religion is explicitly included as one of the characteristics defining a protected group, alongside race, gender, sexual orientation, and disability.
findings: The created dataset, GAHD, contains examples of hate speech targeting religious groups, specifically identifying a cluster of 'anti-Semitic hate speech' and another cluster 'discussing Islam and Muslims'. The paper demonstrates that training a model on the full GAHD dataset significantly improves robustness in detecting hate speech, including that directed at religious groups, with performance increases of 18-20 percentage points on the GAHD and HateCheck test sets.
